title: Project Northstar — Final Steering Committee
subtitle: Decision on a 90-day treasury transformation mobilization · 24 August 2026

slides.title: Authorize 90 days to make the next treasury decision
slides.subtitle: Federated coordination · local-stabilization fallback · no production or funding authorization
slides.notes: Decision requested: authorize evidence mobilization, named owners, G0–G6 gates, and the explicit fallback. Day 90 returns for a separate stop / extend / bounded-pilot decision. Nothing in this deck authorizes production change, cash movement, account closure, labor action, procurement, spend, benefit recognition, or scale. Classification: Confidential — simulated client material.

slides.title: ACG has enough evidence to choose a direction—not enough to approve value or production
slides.subtitle: The first commitment is ownership and controlled evidence
bullets: Choose the federated design direction and seven evidence workstreams.
Keep all production, funding, cash, closure, labor, and value decisions behind later gates.
slides.notes: This is the conclusion loop. The diagnostic numbers create urgency and direction but not investment authority. Visibility is a calendar-date proxy. Payment metrics are within the supplied extract. The option score is analyst judgment. Zero recognized value is an evidence-control status, not a claim of zero opportunity or risk.
sources: W2 visibility/payment diagnostics; W3 option/value models

slides.title: Four linked failures explain ACG's treasury problem
slides.subtitle: The recommendation must fix ownership, evidence, control, and service together
rows: Certify mobility, buffers, economics before action
Local practices; three ERPs; no enterprise TMS
Federated policy/data/control spine with local rights
slides.caption: Implication: a platform alone cannot resolve missing ownership, definitions, controls, and local decision rights.
slides.notes: The four failures form the system map for the rest of the deck. The slide does not claim that technology is unimportant; it places integration behind a governed operating model. Stakeholder statements are corroborating context, not proof.
sources: W2 diagnostic report; W3 future-state operating model

slides.title: Portal and spreadsheet sources explain every delayed account-day in the supplied pattern
slides.subtitle: Automated sources are same-day under the proxy; manual sources are not
slides.caption: 23 manual sources · 58.18% proxy · calendar-date only
slides.notes: The source-method concentration makes the first intervention testable: controlled source, receipt timestamp, balance type, owner, and exception. It does not prove that the method itself is causal; method can proxy for entity, bank, process, or data ownership.

slides.title: The liquidity analysis defines a certification agenda—not a cash-release claim
slides.subtitle: 14-day screen pass rates fall from 100% to 0% as the threshold rises
slides.caption: 168 windows · $0 recognized cash · VG01–VG05 open
slides.notes: The base $35m screen passes 138 of 168 complete windows. The slide avoids the word available. An account enters a funding decision only after current source, restriction, buffer, local/service context, timing, economics, authority, and Finance evidence close.

slides.title: Payment friction is material enough to diagnose—and too weakly evidenced to automate broadly
slides.subtitle: Within the supplied 7,600-record extract
bullets: Use the 120-record purposive frame to link source documents, reason codes, criticality, approvals, and event timing.
Select an intervention only after a consistent, remediable cause and a like-for-like baseline are established.
slides.notes: Manual-touch records have higher exception and late-release rates than non-manual records, but association is not causality. The 120-record frame contains four mutually exclusive cohorts and is designed for root-cause evidence, not prevalence, enterprise extrapolation, or a benefit claim.

slides.title: Six measures tell management whether this is working
slides.subtitle: Each root cause requires an owner and an observable control

quadrants.title: Process & service
quadrants.body: Variable intake, cutoffs, repair loops and emergency practice.

slides.summary_callout: Do not automate an undefined process or centralize an uncertified decision right.
slides.notes: The maturity implication is qualitative: the operating model is fragmented across the four root-cause domains. The deck does not claim technology is causal. It assigns technology as an enabler after ownership, source, process, service, and control rules are explicit.
sources: W2 process/RACI and maturity heatmap; stakeholder pack

slides.title: Eight design principles resolve the tension between enterprise control and local responsiveness
slides.subtitle: Critical gates remain non-compensating

quadrants.title: Enterprise spine
quadrants.body: Daily evidence · global ownership · common policy · controlled metrics

quadrants.title: Local rights
quadrants.body: Certified context · local rights · visible exceptions

quadrants.title: Control by design
quadrants.body: SoD · access · audit · reconciliation · service · resilience · rollback

quadrants.title: Staged and reversible
quadrants.body: Existing ERPs · bounded cohorts · gates · rollback · local fallback

slides.summary_callout: Any failed critical gate blocks the affected decision; value cannot compensate.
slides.notes: The full eight principles are client service, daily evidence, federated decision rights, standardization with exceptions, control, resilient staged integration, data ownership, and scalable acquisition readiness. This slide groups them into four board-level design choices.
sources: W3 design principles and operating model

slides.title: Federated coordination offers the best balance with a local fallback
slides.subtitle: Weighted option score / 100; scores select direction, not execution readiness
slides.caption: 5/5 sensitivity wins · 0 gates closed · switch on failure
slides.notes: The option criteria and weights were locked before scoring. Scores are analyst judgment and do not include diagnostic benefit quantities. Global coordination remains on hold until legal/local, architecture, cyber/resilience, service, cost, mobility, and rollback evidence materially closes.

slides.title: The target model centralizes standards and evidence—not every operational decision
slides.subtitle: One enterprise spine with governed regional and local execution

left.title: Global spine
body: Treasury: policy, data, position and mobility standards
CIO: integration, access, audit, cyber and resilience
Finance: cost/benefit admission and change control

right.title: Regional and local rights
body: Regions/BU: context, requests, critical service and emergencies
Shared Services: payment execution and exceptions

slides.verdict: Internal Audit remains independent; Legal/Tax owns specialist conclusions; every production pilot requires a separate go/no-go.
slides.notes: The model addresses local concerns by making context and emergency rights explicit instead of informal. One accountable owner remains required per activity. Global policy ownership does not transfer every execution step to headquarters.

slides.title: Seven initiatives start with data, governance, and value control—not platform procurement
slides.subtitle: Priority score combines value 30%, risk 25%, feasibility 20%, dependency 15%, speed 10%
slides.caption: Scores order work; no score compensates for a failed critical gate.
slides.notes: I01, I07 and I06 start together because controlled data, value governance and decision rights are dependencies for all other work. Account rationalization ranks last because its direct fee case is modest, although it can progress quickly and safely with per-account validation.

slides.title: The business case stays credible by keeping unlike value types separate
slides.subtitle: Current validated, funded, and recognized value remains zero
slides.caption: Do not add rows. Provisional cost: $755k / $1.155m / $1.715m one-time; $175k / $281k / $442k recurring per year. All costs are analyst assumptions.
slides.notes: The base one-time planning amount fits the $1.0–$1.5m disclosed ceiling; the high case exceeds it by $215k. The base recurring amount is $281k per year and needs separate budget approval. ROI, NPV and payback remain unavailable because recognized benefits and actual cost/timing inputs are absent.
sources: W3 business-case/value/cost outputs; W4 benefits tracker

slides.title: Use 90 days to earn a bounded test before scaling
slides.subtitle: Day 90 is a decision gate—not a launch date

milestones.label: 0–30d
milestones.title: Own the facts
milestones.body: Lock populations, sources, owners and baselines.

milestones.label: 31–60d
milestones.title: Prove conditions
milestones.body: Close local, control, architecture and cost gaps.

milestones.label: 61–90d
milestones.title: Make ready
milestones.body: Prepare cohort gates, controls, rollback and freeze path.

milestones.label: M4–6
milestones.title: Wave 1
milestones.body: Separate approvals; bounded visibility and safe change.

milestones.label: M7–12
milestones.title: Wave 2
milestones.body: Scale only where cash and payment evidence holds.

milestones.label: M13–18
milestones.title: BAU
milestones.body: Embed ownership, support, controls and assurance.

slides.notes: The sequence is dependency-led. Any delay in critical evidence moves later dates right without weakening the gate. North America production routing or approval-workflow change cannot occur in the confirmed eight-week Q4 freeze and requires Rachel Kim's sign-off; exact dates remain open. Month 5 is the earliest realistic NA production planning floor.
sources: W4 roadmap/stage-gate outputs; NA freeze constraint

slides.title: Governance converts the roadmap into stop, switch, and scale decisions
slides.subtitle: Critical risk cannot be averaged away
rows: Narrow, extend with owner/date, or switch
slides.caption: Monthly Steering Committee · weekly Transformation Office · workstream forums · BAU Treasury Operating Council.
slides.notes: The governance system separates workstream management from gate authority. Finance Benefits admits value. Management control owners approve control design. Internal Audit remains independent. A program cannot remain indefinitely amber: G2 and G3 require an explicit decision.

slides.subtitle: Five Steering Committee commitments activate the mobilization
